title: How to Write a Video Brief for Editors and Video Creators
h1: How to write a video brief for editors and video creators
description: What to include in a video brief: goal, audience, platform and format, length, footage and assets, style references, music, captions, revisions and deadlines.
intro: Video projects involve many choices: length, pace, music, text, colors, format and where the video will be shown. When those choices are left to the editor, the first draft often misses the mark and revisions pile up. A clear video brief answers the important questions before work starts. This article explains what to include, whether you are hiring an editor for existing footage, an animator or a videographer to film something new.

faq.q: How long should a video brief be?
faq.a: One or two pages is usually enough, plus links to footage and examples.

faq.q: Should I write the script myself?
faq.a: If the message matters, yes or with a scriptwriter. Editors shape footage; they do not usually write the message.
Agree in advance. Use licensed music, and keep the license details with the project.

faq.q: What if I do not know what style I want?
faq.a: Collect a few videos you like and dislike and explain why. Patterns usually appear.

faq.q: Do I get the project files?
faq.a: Not always by default. Ask early if you want editable project files.
